title: Complexity map of the simple Kerr MLP (window x width)
question: Which simple Kerr MLP is best in 100-40 000 RM, and where do a window wider than 31 or depth pay off?
git_commit: recorded per run in results/runs/*.json (field git_commit); rule commit: see LOG.md
eval_rule: validation and (report-only) test every max(500, steps/40) steps; selection only by validation

confirm.rule: Pareto front by (RM, mean validation at 100k); more than 12 -> 12 spread evenly in log RM

instability: share of diverged seeds per window (E012: windows 65 and 127 unstable)

rule_draft.status: DRAFT: to be confirmed by the user before the first run; must not change after results are seen
rule_draft.width: a window wider than 31 pays off at a given RM if best(w) for w > 31 is higher than best(w = 31) by >= 0.5 p.p. (3 seeds, intervals do not overlap); RM bins: +-25 % log windows of results/pareto levels
rule_draft.depth: depth (both) pays off if both is better than one_hidden at equal RM (same bin) by >= 0.5 p.p.
rule_draft.saturation: the smallest RM after which doubling RM gives < 0.5 p.p. (envelope of the validation means)
rule_draft.noise: thresholds in p.p. are compared with results/noise_floor.json (E024): MDD(5 seeds) = t_{0.975,8} * s_pooled * sqrt(2/5); 0.1 dB of Q2 = 6 p.p. at 10 %, 4.1 at 48 %, 3.0 at 66 %, 2.7 at 70 % (anchors); every table prints both
